notes: Root cause (G11 A/B + code): handle_tcp copied every RX segment into the fixed 4 MiB per-socket ring (SOCKET_RX_BUF_SIZE) with no overflow guard and ACKed it all; a body >= ~4 MiB ahead of the app drain wrapped the ring and overwrote unread data -> open-fail 'Unsupported protocol', bytes=0, server/port/content independent. Fix = producer flow control on the existing ring (memory unchanged): (1) store only contiguous expected payload that fits free space, ACK only stored bytes, refuse out-of-order/overflow (counted rx_drops); (2) advertise the true free TCP window (removed the min-2048 floor; window 0 when full; post-drain window-update ACK reopens); (3) honor FIN only at the contiguous stream end. Ring size is now latency slack, not the correctness bound; documented in src/kernel/net.c + continuation/fs-n3/README.md. Retest on identity wire (no gzip): 6 MiB blob and CNN 5,704,241 B both complete with byte-match copy-backs; small/head controls pass; flow-control guard engaged with 0 drops (peer self-paced). Regression sweep green: SOCK2TST 35 PASS, DNSTST A-record, NETFIX ALL PASS, unit-arm 302/0, unit-x64 KVM 306/0, ARM wave 0-FAIL.
